section_summary.extract_value: Abstract of a single study reporting that self-compassion buffered the negative relationships between two body-related threats (body comparison and appearance-contingent self-worth) and body appreciation. The study used an online sample of 263 women (Mage = 35.26, SD = 12.42) and found that when self-compassion was high these threats were unrelated to body appreciation, whereas when self-compassion was low the relationships were strong.
section_summary.evidence_source: Full abstract text: "Although research on positive body image has increased, little research has explored which variables protect body appreciation during body-related threats. ... In this study, we investigated whether two body-related threats ... among an online sample of 263 women (Mage = 35.26, SD = 12.42). Results indicated that self-compassion moderated the inverse relationships between body related threats and body appreciation. Specifically, when self-compassion was very high, body comparison and appearance contingent self-worth were unrelated to body appreciation. However, when self-compassion was low, these relationships were strong."
